neighbours.label: the virama (halant / pulli) joining a consonant cluster inside a word in an Indic script (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil)
fire: In yoga the word for knowledge is vidya (विद्या), and it is often paired with practice.
Devotion, or bhakti (भक्ति), is one of the paths described in the old poems.
Visitors are greeted with the word namaste (नमस्ते) at the door of the school.
The priest recited a short mantra (मन्त्र) before the lamp was lit.
The Bengali word for friend is bondhu (বন্ধু) and the word for story is golpo (গল্প).
The Tamil word for thanks is nandri (நன்றி), which travellers learn first.
The fire god is called Agni (अग्नि) and the word for book is pustak (पुस्तक).
The Hindi word for welcome is swagat (स्वागत), printed on the banner above the gate.
quiet: In the village the word for water is pani (पानी), and it is heard at every well.
The name, or naam (नाम), is written on the first page of the old ledger.
Visitors are greeted with the word annyeong (안녕) at the door of the school.
The priest recited a short blessing (ευλογία) before the lamp was lit.
The Bengali word for river is nodi (নদী) and the word for water is jol (জল).
The Thai word for thanks is khop khun (ขอบคุณ), which travellers learn first.
The Hindi word for day is din (दिन) and the word for fruit is phal (फल).
The Russian word for welcome is privet (привет), printed on the banner above the gate.

notes: Card: top 32 peaks are byte pieces of '्' / '্' inside conjuncts (चित्त, হেমন্ত, अक्षय), plus Korean and Hebrew-point outliers. Probes: Devanagari / Bengali / Tamil words with a virama 0.48-0.75; घर (no virama) 0.01, Korean 0.01, pointed Hebrew 0.15. Fire items each contain Indic words with conjuncts; near misses use Indic words without a virama or other non-Latin scripts.
